name: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-17

card.summary: A cosmetic peptide in lash and brow serums, marketed to support keratin and follicle activity for longer, fuller-looking lashes and brows.
card.note: Sold as a cosmetic ingredient; supplier claims are not backed by published human trials.

quick.overview:
Palmitoyl pentapeptide-17 is a short cosmetic peptide used in lash and brow serums. The lash-grade ingredient is usually listed as myristoyl pentapeptide-17.

People apply it along the lash line or brows hoping for longer, thicker-looking lashes and brows, and it also appears in some anti-aging products.
quick.mechanism: Suppliers say it supports keratin synthesis and hair-follicle activity. These statements come from suppliers and are based on laboratory work.
quick.risks: It is a topical cosmetic ingredient used at very low concentrations. As with any eye-area product, irritation is the main practical concern.

lead: Palmitoyl pentapeptide-17 is a cosmetic signal peptide, a short chain of five amino acids joined to a fatty acid so that it can sit in a water-based serum and be applied to the skin. It is associated with lash and brow serums, which people use hoping for longer, fuller-looking lashes and brows. The lash-and-brow ingredient sold by suppliers is usually listed under the INCI name Myristoyl Pentapeptide-17, a closely named variant with a myristic rather than palmitic fatty-acid tail, and the two names are often used interchangeably in discussion.[1]

The supplier page describes the peptide as stimulating keratin synthesis and supporting follicle activity, and lists benefits claimed for consumers as longer-looking, fuller lashes, stronger roots and reduced fallout.[1] It is offered for eyelash serums, eyebrow growth serums, lash conditioners and primers, and mascaras and brow products with treatment claims.[1]
The supplier page publishes no study results, concentrations or safety data, and no published human trial of the ingredient was found.

chain: Peptide serum applied to the lash line or brows
Marketed to support keratin synthesis and follicle activity
Longer, fuller-looking lashes and brows over weeks of use
angle.text: People use serums containing this peptide on the lash line or brows hoping for longer, thicker-looking lashes and brows. Suppliers attribute this to keratin and follicle support.

infobox: Lash serums, brow serums, lash conditioners, mascaras[1]

paras: The peptide is listed for eyelash serums, lash conditioners and primers, eyebrow growth serums, and mascaras and brow products with treatment claims.[1]

The supplier states that the peptide enhances lash and brow growth by stimulating keratin synthesis and supporting follicle activity, and lists follicle growth markers VEGF, beta-catenin, bFGF and collagen III as upregulated.[1] It also lists antioxidant protection, reduced inflammation around follicles and protection against environmental stress.[1] These statements are the supplier's, and the page gives no models or statistics behind them.[1]

The supplier page gives no toxicology or irritation data and links to a safety data sheet that was not reviewed.[1] It is a topical cosmetic ingredient, and product labels for eye-area products generally carry irritation guidance.
